name: The Relay Works
reading: Surge's town keeps the power, the relays and the storm gear running (docs/world-building/TOWN_CHARACTER.md gym3_town: deepslate and tuff, weathered and waxed copper). The substation where the feeder from his array lands, walked through: in at the west door on the lane, past the cable drums, up the transformer bank's stair onto the catwalk, where three leads run out to three bus bars over a floor of packing straw (only the west lead is whole, and the bright copper and the lamps over its bar say so), along the live bar across the open isolator, through the wall by the duct and down; then in at the south end of the Grounding Hall, three courses under the works' floor by one broad stair, where the line is earthed: transformer banks on both walls, each a stage further up the copper's oxidation ladder, three bus runs hung on chains overhead, lightning rods on every bank, and down the floor a single course of waxed copper that is oxidised at the stair and bright at the cab, with a pair of ochre lights set in the floor every third course: the signal line the player walks. Surge stands in a control cab four courses up at the north end, between a generator housing and a pilaster, in front of a board of redstone lamps whose lit columns rise to a peak over his head. No colonnade, no nave: machinery on both walls, a line in the floor and a board behind him. Every copper block is waxed, so the gradient stays where it is put.

battle.why: Cobblemon Battle Positions (see data/gym_arenas/gym1.json battle.why): the Pokemon blocks one under the floor's top course, under the copper line so they are under full blocks. Surge's Pokemon is 5.5 from the cab's face (cell edge z1433.0 against block centre z1427.5; clear radius 2.93, Raichu's model sweep: 2.57 to spare) and 6.5 from the nearest bank (the cell edge x1742 against x1748.5); the challenger's is 7 behind it, which is the larger of the two Pokemon being 1.5 wide at most (Vikavolt) with the whole of Raichu's 2.93 sweep as well; the challenger stands 3 behind their own. The trainer stand is under the cab top one in front of the seat, so Surge steps to the cab's edge.

entry.why: street is the lane cell west of the door (ground y174 at x1721, tools/ground.py rounded: the lane runs flat along the foot of the wall, so the street is level with the works' floor). entry.floor is the Grounding Hall's first floor cell below the broad stair, 29 from Surge: farther than rctmod's forceBattleMaxDistance + 1 = 17, so the player stands on the hall floor before he can call the fight.

exit.why: the door past the leader: an iron door in the divider at the cab's west side, onto the bay ten blocks from the street door, opened by the stone button on the hall side of the wall (the stair up to it is beside the cab). Nothing in the bay opens it, so it cannot be used to reach Surge past the tower, the bars and the juniors. Or back the way you came: every step of the walk is a half step or a one-block step, nothing one-way.

blocks_why: the town's own palette (TOWN_CHARACTER.md gym3_town: deepslate and tuff, weathered and waxed copper) and nothing else of the world's: no grass, leaves, water, sand or carpet. Every copper block is WAXED: an unwaxed one oxidises over time, and the whole point of the gradient (and of the clue on the bars) is that it stays where it is put. The lightning rods and redstone lamps are spawn-condition blocks (data/spawn_blocks.json: lightning rod for Electrode, Galvantula, Joltik; redstone lamp for Rotom), kept from the carved Grounding Hall for its look; the whole lot is inside the spawn-free zone gym_surge, so they decide no encounter. The lamps are lit only with a redstone block touching them (an unpowered lit lamp switches itself off a few ticks after a neighbour changes). Hay is straw on a stone floor, inside a roofed hall.
